_comment: U7 LG1 + LG2 (docs/specs/ATP_LEGENDS_SCREENS_ADDENDUM.md): the Legends cards (LG1: the first eight; LG2 and LG3, marked 'slice': 'lg2' / 'lg3', each behind its own flag on top of screener_legends) - each a short card about a publicly described trading method and a working ScreenQL screen modelled on it. A reviewed data file: change it by PR. app/screener/legends.py lints it on load: every card line cites a source in legends_sources.json, at most 5 lines, no advice / performance / endorsement wording, no first person or quotation, no trademarked method name in a title, English only, and the screen compiles with its parameters inside their documented ranges. Each card id is a screen filed in taxonomy.json (method Legends) - the taxonomy CI guard fails when it is not. The disclaimer is fixed in code (spec wording), never per card. Each card carries a review status (LG1-2): 'verified' when every source it cites is verified against public catalogue records (legends_sources.json 'evidence'), else 'unverified' with a 'review_note' saying why; the API exposes it. The owner's legal review of the card texts is separate.

cards.name: Minervini-style trend template

who.text: US stock trader who set out his approach in the 2013 book Trade Like a Stock Market Wizard.

style.text: Trend following in stocks: a stock qualifies only when a checklist of price and moving-average conditions shows a long-term uptrend.

looks_for.text: Price above the 50, 150 and 200-day averages in that order, a rising 200-day, near the 52-week high, well off the low, high relative strength.

timeframe.text: Daily bars; a trend filter applied before looking for a base and a breakout.

cards.approximation: Relative strength here is the percentile of the 250-bar % change within the scanned list, not a published rating; 52 weeks = 250 bars; rising = above its value 21 bars ago.

screen.source: close > SMA(close, 50) AND SMA(close, 50) > SMA(close, 150) AND SMA(close, 150) > SMA(close, 200) AND SMA(close, 200) > SMA(close, 200)[21] AND close >= $near_high * Max(high, 250) AND close >= $above_low * Min(low, 250) AND PercentileRank(PctChange(close, 250)) >= $rs_min

params.name: near_high
params.doc: Close at least this fraction of the 52-week high (0.75 = within 25% of it).

params.name: above_low
params.doc: Close at least this multiple of the 52-week low (1.3 = 30% above it).

params.name: rs_min
params.doc: Lowest relative-strength percentile within the scanned list.

cards.name: Darvas-style box breakout

who.text: Professional dancer who described the stock-trading method he used in a 1960 book.

style.text: Box theory: a rising stock moves through a series of price boxes; he acted only when price rose out of the top of the latest box.

looks_for.text: A close above a tight consolidation (the box) to a new high for the period, on volume above its recent average, near the 52-week high.

timeframe.text: Daily bars; positions held while price keeps forming higher boxes.

cards.approximation: The box here is the high and low of the previous 20 bars, at most 15% deep; the book draws its boxes by eye from daily highs and lows.

screen.source: close > Max(high, $box_bars)[1] AND Min(low, $box_bars)[1] >= $box_floor * Max(high, $box_bars)[1] AND volume >= $vol_mult * SMA(volume, 50)[1] AND close >= $near_high * Max(high, 250)

params.name: box_bars
params.doc: Bars that make up the box before today.

params.name: box_floor
params.doc: Box low at least this fraction of the box high (0.85 = at most 15% deep).

params.name: vol_mult
params.doc: Volume at least this multiple of its 50-bar average.

params.name: near_high
params.doc: Close at least this fraction of the 52-week high.

cards.name: Weinstein-style stage 2 breakout

who.text: Technical analyst who described stage analysis in a 1988 book on bull and bear markets.

style.text: Stage analysis: a stock moves through four stages (base, advance, top, decline), read on the weekly chart and its 30-week moving average.

looks_for.text: A weekly close above the prior base high and above a flat or rising 30-week average, on volume well above its recent average.

timeframe.text: Weekly bars; positional holding periods of months.

cards.approximation: The base here is the high of the previous 10 weeks; flat or rising = the 30-week average not below its value 1 and 4 weeks ago; volume vs the 4 weeks before; no relative-strength check yet.

screen.source: close > SMA(close, 30) AND SMA(close, 30) >= SMA(close, 30)[1] AND SMA(close, 30) >= SMA(close, 30)[4] AND close > Max(high, $base_weeks)[1] AND volume >= $vol_mult * SMA(volume, 4)[1]

params.name: base_weeks
params.doc: Weeks of base before this week.

params.name: vol_mult
params.doc: Weekly volume at least this multiple of the 4 weeks before.

cards.legend: Richard Dennis, William Eckhardt and the Turtle traders
cards.name: Turtle-style 20-day channel breakout

who.text: Traders trained in the 1980s by Richard Dennis and William Eckhardt; former Turtles later published the rules.

style.text: Systematic trend following: entries on channel breakouts, with position size and stops set from volatility (N, an average true range).

looks_for.text: The day's high above the highest high of the previous 20 days (System 1); System 2 used 55 days.

timeframe.text: Daily bars; trades lasting days to months; the rules were written for futures markets.

cards.approximation: Long side only here (the rules were symmetric); System 1's filter that skips a breakout after a winning one is not included.

params.name: entry_days
params.doc: Channel length in days (20 = System 1, 55 = System 2).

cards.legend: Linda Bradford Raschke and Laurence Connors
cards.name: Raschke-style ADX pullback to the 20 EMA

who.text: Futures trader; co-author with Laurence Connors of the 1995 book Street Smarts.

style.text: Short-term pullbacks in strong trends, with the ADX used to judge trend strength.

looks_for.text: ADX(14) above 30 and a pullback whose low touches the 20-period EMA after trading above it; the trigger is a move above the pullback bar's high.

timeframe.text: Daily bars; a short-term setup lasting days.

cards.approximation: An uptrend here is a 20-period EMA above its value 5 bars ago; ADX rising beforehand is not checked; long side only; the screen lists the touch, and the trigger bar is left for the trader to watch.

screen.source: ADX(14) > $adx_min AND EMA(close, 20) > EMA(close, 20)[5] AND low <= EMA(close, 20) AND low[1] > EMA(close, 20)[1]

params.name: adx_min
params.doc: Lowest ADX(14) reading that counts as a strong trend.

cards.name: Crabel-style NR7 range contraction

who.text: Trader and author of a 1990 statistical study of short-term price patterns and the opening-range breakout.

style.text: Short-term patterns studied statistically, such as range contraction and breakouts from the opening range.

looks_for.text: An NR7 day: today's high-low range is narrower than that of each of the previous six days (range contraction).

timeframe.text: Daily bars; the follow-through is studied over the next session.

cards.approximation: The screen lists NR7 days in either direction; the opening-range breakout that follows needs intraday bars and is not part of it.

params.name: prior_days
params.doc: Previous days today's range must be narrower than (6 = NR7, 3 = NR4).

cards.name: Connors-style 2-period RSI pullback
cards.review_note: Its source connors_alvarez_2008 is unverified: catalogues disagree on the first-edition year (2008 or 2009), which the who line states.

who.text: Author of books on short-term trading, including a 2008 study written with Cesar Alvarez.

style.text: Short-term mean reversion: brief pullbacks inside long-term uptrends, measured with a 2-period RSI.

looks_for.text: Close above the 200-day simple moving average and a 2-period RSI below 10, a deep short-term oversold reading.

timeframe.text: Daily bars; trades lasting a few days.

cards.approximation: The book examines several RSI(2) thresholds and exits; the screen lists the setup only, with the threshold editable.

params.name: rsi_max
params.doc: 2-period RSI below this reading.

cards.name: Williams-style volatility breakout

who.text: Futures trader and author of the 1999 book Long-Term Secrets to Short-Term Trading.

style.text: Short-term volatility breakouts: a move away from the day's open by part of the previous day's range.

looks_for.text: The day's high reaching the open plus a fraction (default 0.5) of the previous day's high-low range.

timeframe.text: Daily bars; very short-term trades of one to a few days.

cards.approximation: On end-of-day bars the screen checks the day's high; long side only; the book examines several fractions and range measures (editable here).

params.name: k
params.doc: Fraction of the previous day's range added to the open.

cards.name: Livermore-style pivotal-point breakout
cards.review_note: Cites livermore_1940, whose first-edition details are not yet matched to a library catalogue record.

who.text: US stock and commodity speculator of the early 20th century who set out his method in the 1940 book How to Trade in Stocks.

style.text: Waiting for confirmation: acting only when price moves decisively through a pivotal point, with volume rising, and never adding to a losing position.

looks_for.text: A close above the top of a long sideways base to a new 52-week high, on volume well above its recent average.

timeframe.text: Daily bars; moves followed over weeks to months.

cards.approximation: The pivotal point here is the high of the previous 60 bars and the base is at most 25% deep; a 52-week high stands in for a new high; the book's time element and its records are not part of it.

screen.source: close > Max(high, $base_bars)[1] AND Min(low, $base_bars)[1] >= $base_floor * Max(high, $base_bars)[1] AND close > Max(high, 250)[1] AND volume >= $vol_mult * SMA(volume, 50)[1]

params.name: base_bars
params.doc: Bars that make up the base before today; its high is the pivotal point.

params.name: base_floor
params.doc: Base low at least this fraction of the base high (0.75 = at most 25% deep).

params.name: vol_mult
params.doc: Volume at least this multiple of its 50-bar average.

cards.name: Wyckoff-style trading-range spring

who.text: Early 20th-century US market author and educator whose method of reading trading ranges is set out in a 2007 book on trading skills.

style.text: Reading a sideways range as accumulation or distribution from price and volume, before the trend that follows it.

looks_for.text: Within a sideways range, a dip below the range's low that closes back inside the range (a spring), a test of whether supply is exhausted.

timeframe.text: Daily bars; the range forms over weeks before the move out of it.

cards.approximation: The range here is the previous 40 bars, at most 20% deep; a spring is a low under the range's low with a close back above it; the volume reading and the later test of the spring are not part of it.

screen.source: Min(low, $range_bars)[1] >= $range_floor * Max(high, $range_bars)[1] AND low < Min(low, $range_bars)[1] AND close > Min(low, $range_bars)[1]

params.name: range_bars
params.doc: Bars that make up the trading range before today.

params.name: range_floor
params.doc: Range low at least this fraction of the range high (0.8 = at most 20% deep).

cards.legend: Linda Bradford Raschke and Laurence Connors
cards.name: Raschke-style false 20-day breakdown reversal

who.text: Futures trader; co-author with Laurence Connors of the 1995 book Street Smarts.

style.text: Short-term reversals: fading a new 20-day extreme that fails, when the previous extreme is some days old.

looks_for.text: A new 20-day low while the previous 20-day low is at least four sessions old, with price back above that earlier low the same day.

timeframe.text: Daily bars; a short-term setup lasting a few days.

cards.approximation: Long side only here; the book's entry order just above the earlier low is read as the day's high reaching above it; the variant a day later and the short-side mirror are not included.

screen.source: low < Min(low, $channel_days)[1] AND Min(low, $recent_bars)[1] > Min(low, $channel_days)[1] AND high > Min(low, $channel_days)[1]

params.name: channel_days
params.doc: Days of the low that today breaks (20 in the book).

params.name: recent_bars
params.doc: The earlier low is older than this many bars (3 = at least four sessions before today).

cards.name: Crabel-style opening-range breakout

who.text: Trader and author of a 1990 statistical study of short-term price patterns and the opening-range breakout.

style.text: Short-term patterns studied statistically, such as range contraction and breakouts from the opening range.

looks_for.text: An intraday close crossing above the high of the session's opening range, the range of its first 30 minutes.

timeframe.text: Intraday 5-minute bars; the move is studied within the same session.

cards.approximation: The level here is the high of the first 30 minutes; the book's own breakout levels, measured from the open, and the downside break are not part of it.

params.name: or_minutes
params.doc: Minutes from the session open that make up the opening range.

cards.name: Tudor Jones-style 200-day regime filter

who.text: US macro trader and fund manager, interviewed about his risk rules in a 2014 book on investing.

style.text: Defence first: every market is judged against its 200-day moving average of closing prices, and what falls below it is left.

looks_for.text: A close above its 200-day simple moving average: the symbols in the long-side regime, as a context filter for other screens.

timeframe.text: Daily bars; a regime that changes slowly.

cards.approximation: Only the regime is screened; the interview describes the average as a rule for when to be out of a market, not an entry signal, and gives no further rules.

params.name: ma_days
params.doc: Days in the simple moving average of closing prices (200 in the interview).

cards.name: Graham-style net current asset bargain
cards.review_note: Cites graham_1949 and graham_dodd_1934, whose first editions are not yet matched to a library catalogue record.

who.text: US investor and teacher of security analysis who set out value-investing principles in books of 1934 and 1949.

style.text: Value investing with a margin of safety: buying a business for well under a conservative estimate of its worth.

looks_for.text: A price at or below two-thirds of net current asset value per share: current assets minus all liabilities, per share.

timeframe.text: Daily prices against the latest reported balance sheet; holdings kept for months to years.

cards.approximation: Uses the balance sheet known on each day (point in time, never a later restatement); the books also ask for a diversified group of such issues and for some earnings, which the screen does not check.

params.name: ncav_frac
params.doc: Price at most this fraction of net current asset value per share (0.67 = two-thirds).

cards.name: Graham-style defensive value (Graham number)
cards.review_note: Cites graham_1949, whose first edition is not yet matched to a library catalogue record.

who.text: US investor and teacher of security analysis who set out a policy for the defensive investor in a 1949 book.

style.text: Defensive value: a moderate price against both earnings and book value, with a margin of safety.

looks_for.text: A price below the Graham number, the square root of 22.5 x earnings per share x book value per share.

timeframe.text: Daily prices against the latest reported earnings and balance sheet; a long holding period.

cards.approximation: 22.5 is 15 times earnings times 1.5 times book; trailing earnings are the last four reported quarters (or the last year), as known on each day; the book's size, dividend and earnings-stability tests are not checked.

params.name: margin
params.doc: Price below this fraction of the Graham number (1.0 = below it at all).

cards.name: Greenblatt-style earnings yield and return on capital rank

who.text: US investor and teacher who described a ranking method in a 2006 book written for general readers.

style.text: Quantitative value: good businesses at bargain prices, ranked on two measures and bought as a group.

looks_for.text: A high combined rank on earnings yield (EBIT / enterprise value) and return on capital within the scanned list.

timeframe.text: Daily prices with the latest reported figures; the book holds each position for about a year.

cards.approximation: Ranks within the scanned list, not the whole market; capital is total assets minus current liabilities and cash (the book uses net working capital plus net fixed assets); financials and utilities are not excluded.

screen.source: EarningsYield() > 0 AND ReturnOnCapital() > 0 AND PercentileRank(EarningsYield()) + PercentileRank(ReturnOnCapital()) >= $rank_sum

params.name: rank_sum
params.doc: Lowest sum of the two percentile ranks (each 0 to 100) within the scanned list.

cards.name: O'Neil-style growth breakout

who.text: US investor and publisher who described a growth-stock method in a 1988 book.

style.text: Growth with price leadership: strong current earnings and sales growth, bought as the price breaks to new highs.

looks_for.text: Quarterly EPS and sales well up on the same quarter a year before, and a close at a new 52-week high on volume well above average.

timeframe.text: Daily bars and the latest reported quarter; positions held while the trend lasts.

cards.approximation: Growth is the latest quarter known on each day (point in time); the base pattern, the relative-strength rating, market direction and institutional sponsorship in the book are not checked.

screen.source: EPSGrowthYoY() >= $eps_min AND SalesGrowthYoY() >= $sales_min AND close > Max(high, 250)[1] AND volume >= $vol_mult * SMA(volume, 50)[1]

params.name: eps_min
params.doc: Lowest growth of quarterly EPS on the same quarter a year before, %.

params.name: sales_min
params.doc: Lowest growth of quarterly sales on the same quarter a year before, %.

params.name: vol_mult
params.doc: Volume at least this multiple of its 50-bar average (1.5 = 50% above).
